# Computer Science > Computation and Language

[Submitted on 31 Aug 2026]

# Title: Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation

Authors: Alessio Galatolo , Meriem Beloucif

View a PDF of the paper titled Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation, by Alessio Galatolo and 1 other authors

View PDF HTML (experimental)

> Abstract: Adapting large language models to user-specific preferences is often constrained by the cost of human annotation, making preference optimisation impractical in low-resource settings where preferences cannot be reliably labelled by LLMs themselves, e.g., due to cultural, subjective, or personalised contexts. In this paper, we investigate how language models encode preference information in their intermediate representations, finding that activations from chosen and rejected responses form distinct clusters across layers, even in pretrained models. Strikingly, this structure is strengthened by alignment on canonical datasets but erased when the target preferences differ from those the model was aligned on, suggesting aligned LLMs are poor judges for non-mainstream populations. Exploiting this structure, we propose training a lightweight linear probe on a few labelled preference pairs (≤500) and using it to annotate large unlabelled datasets (50K+) for downstream preference optimisation. We systematically evaluate this approach across different datasets, preference optimisation methods and model scales and find that our method consistently outperforms direct training given the same annotation budget, and remains competitive against baselines trained on 50-100× more labelled data in the majority of our settings. summaryZh: 针对大模型偏好适应中高昂的标注成本问题，该研究提出了一种基于激活的标签传播方法。通过分析模型中间层的激活特征，研究发现偏好信息在预训练模型中已形成可区分的聚类结构。研究者利用少量标注数据训练线性探针，进而对大规模无标注数据进行自动标注，从而实现高效的偏好优化。实验证明该方法在低资源环境下表现优于直接训练，且具有较强的竞争力。
